item.title: [NPR News] Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
item.description:
Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
November 11, 202612:23 PM ET
By
Ricci Shryock
Ricci Shrylock/NPR
Hip-hop music blasted over a portable speaker while half-a-dozen teenagers practiced their best breakdancing moves in Senagal's capital Dakar. They glided on their shins and jumped into the air, clutched their heels and struck midair poses.
Senegal's breakdancers were honing their craft ahead of the country's historic hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month. It's the first time an Olympic event is being held on African soil.
I took the photo above last month as 15-year-old Suzanne Toure struck a breakdancing pose. She is the only girl on the Senegal National Sport Dance and Break Team. Three years ago, her little brother introduced her to breakdancing.
Dancers on the Senegalese team mix traditional moves into their routines from national styles such as mbalax and Yela, swirling their arms and legs in a windmill-like motion. "You can sense some American and European influence in our routines, yes, but there are also African dances. It's about mixing these African dances into the breaking," says coach Francis Siméon Gomis.
They see this as their chance to show the world what their nation can offer on the dance floor, and hope to win a medal on home turf.

item.description:
Islamic State group-affiliated rebels kill at least 22 in Congo's eastern region
A rebel group affiliated with the Islamic State group has killed at least 22 people in Congo's eastern Ituri provinceByJEAN-YVES KAMALE Associated Press and JUSTIN KABUMBA Associated PressNovember 11, 2026, 11:52 AM
ITURI, Congo -- At least 22 people were killed in a series of attacks by a rebel group affiliated with the Islamic State group between Tuesday and Wednesday in Congo 's eastern Ituri province.
The attacks were carried out by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) across eight locations in the Mambasa territory in Ituri, according to two civil society and human rights monitoring groups.
At least 10 people were also abducted.
“The death toll remains provisional. In addition to the 22 civilians killed, the perpetrators abducted other individuals, and motorcycles and homes were set on fire,” said Marie-Noelle Anatobe, coordinator of the Civil Society of Congo in Mambasa territory.
The attacks happened in nearly inaccessible locations near the border between Uganda and Congo.
The ADF grew out of Uganda and was pushed to the border region with Congo, where it has operated for years, targeting civilians. It pledged allegiance to the Islamic State group in 2019.
Both the Ugandan and Congolese armies have been jointly attacking the group, but they have long struggled against it.

"After The Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary's Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase which have now forced the secretary to relocate to a military base for his safety," the person told CBS News.

The severity and nature of the threat against Scott Bessent remains unclearByBernd Debusmann JrWhite House reporter Published11 November 2026, 16:24 GMTUpdated 54 minutes ago
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved from his Washington DC home to a military base after Iran-linked threats to his life, according to US media reports.
CBS, the BBC's US partner, said the relocation came after a photo of Bessent's home was published in the Wall Street Journal.
Bessent has been at the forefront of efforts to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and a wider economic blockade.
While the exact nature of the threats against Bessent remain unclear, US intelligence has warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans, including US officials.
"After the Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary's Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase," a source told CBS.
Georgetown is an affluent part of Washington that is home to a number of government officials and prominent residents.
Those security concerns, the source added, prompted authorities to move Bessent to a military base in the area.
In a statement, a Treasury Department spokesperson said only that Bessent "will not be deterred" by threats and "remains committed" to the US effort to pressure Iran's economy.
The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.
In September, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans.

item.title: [CBS News World] Hoax bomb threats affect at least 20 European flights within hours
item.description:
Paris — At least 20 commercial flights in Europe had to deal with bomb threats Thursday, with at least one being diverted to a military base in France. While authorities have reported no explosives discovered on any of the jets, and they all appeared to be hoaxes, Thursday's incidents add to a fast-growing number of journeys hit by similar threats this week, which one expert said suggested a "very deliberate act."
British authorities dismissed threats to about seven flights earlier this week as hoaxes, but the number of impacted journeys soared to at least 27 on Thursday, meaning significant disruption for thousands of passengers and raising concerns about a possible coordinated effort to impact travel on the continent.
At least two more European flights, along with several Irish and British news outlets, got similar threats on Friday.
No authorities have confirmed a link between any of the threats, but Spanish Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares said Friday that Europe appeared to be facing "hybrid aggression and a form of psychological warfare."
David Kaminski-Morrow, Air Transport Editor with FlightGlobal, declined to speculate on who might be behind the threats to commercial flights this week, but he noted that "we currently live in a time of political aggression in regions including Europe, and it's a pretty effective tactic if someone is looking to cause disruption."
"The cluster of threats seems unusual, but it's hard to determine the extent to which they might be organized," he said, noting that "the publicity alone could spur further threats unrelated to earlier ones."

On Thursday Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Moscow and Dublin to hold talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidentsByLaura GozziPublished2 hours ago
Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day.
Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion.
Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest."
"I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible.
Both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon.
After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.
This latest round of talks had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe.
For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member.
For Moscow, it is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion.
Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system.

Watch: Protesters gather across Spain for first general strike in 14 yearsByNick Beake, Europe correspondent, Reporting fromMadrid, Guy Hedgecoe, Reporting fromMadrid and Alba MorgadePublished11 November 2026, 14:06 GMTUpdated 3 hours ago
Transport and other public services across Spain have faced serious disruption in the first general strike for 14 years called by the main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
Demonstrations were also planned later on Wednesday, with the biggest protests expected in Madrid and Barcelona. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November.
The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant."
However, the Spanish Confederation of Business Organisations said participation was "low and uneven", depending on the areas and sectors involved.
Image source, ReutersImage caption,
The general strike took place little more than two weeks ahead of national elections in Spain
Some of the biggest disruption on Wednesday was seen in the main industrial hubs of Madrid and the north-eastern region of Catalonia where traffic was halted on several main roads.
The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.
The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later.

Nissan reduces petrol car production as EV sales boom in China
Manufacturer says ‘shift to new energy vehicles is happening faster than expected’ and market is harsh
Business live – latest updates
The Japanese carmaker Nissan has said it has been caught out by accelerating sales of electric and hybrid cars in China amid a brutal price war in the world’s biggest automotive market.
The manufacturer slashed its sales forecasts for China and said it would cut back on petrol car manufacturing while increasing production of battery electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, which combine a smaller battery with a petrol engine.
Nissan said it expected to sell between 2.97m and 3m cars this year, down from a previous forecast of 3.15m, mainly because of struggles in China.
“China remains our biggest challenge,” said Ivan Espinosa, Nissan’s chief executive. “Demand is weaker, competition is intensifying, and the shift to new energy vehicles is happening faster than expected. The market is being very, very harsh.”
The company reported increased sales in its home market as well as in North America, regions in which the shift to electric cars has been much slower because of policy decisions, including Donald Trump’s tearing up of incentives for battery car makers.
That divergence between different parts of the world illustrates the challenge for global carmakers, many of whom are trying to continue selling their more profitable petrol and diesel cars for as long as possible while risking being left behind by newer Chinese rivals.
China’s government gave weighty subsidies to its electric car industry, spotting an opportunity to overtake other countries such as Germany, Japan and the US, which had dominated sales of internal combustion engine cars.

Nvidia hires leading US law firm to investigate Jensen Huang’s relationship
Move comes as chipmaker reels from reports its CEO was having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy
Business live – latest updates
Nvidia has appointed a leading US law firm to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation into the relationship between its chief executive, Jensen Huang, and an alleged Chinese spy.
The $4.1tn (£3tn) chipmaker has hired New York-based Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz for the investigation, which will be led by the Wachtell partner Joon Kim. Wachtell’s website describes Kim, a former government prosecutor in New York, as a specialist in areas including internal investigations, white-collar criminal and regulatory defence, and crisis management.
Nvidia did not give a timeframe for the investigation but the company has said Huang will continue to lead the business he co-founded “without interruption”.
The company is reeling from an espionage scandal after reports that its chief executive had been having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, who was also an Nvidia customer.
The US ambassador to China, David Perdue, said: “The situation with Nvidia is another reminder that we have to stay diligent.
“National security is part of this economic conversation because economic security is national security. And so, what we’re doing with China is bumpy right now,” he told Bloomberg Television.
Nvidia had at first denied an improper relationship with the Chinese citizen, who is no relation to the Nvidia boss, but Huang then admitted on Sunday he had been unfaithful to his wife – without referring directly to Ms Huang.

Germany’s drone ban, effective immediately, follows the US military banning China’s BYD electric vehicles from its Kadena airbase on the Japanese island of Okinawa. Local commanders had been allowed to buy the drones under ‌a 2024 strategy that included a “white list” of approved systems, including several made by the ​China-based DJI, the world’s largest drone maker.
As there is no central record of purchases by individual units, the military has to ⁠impose a blanket ban, Der Spiegel reported.

item.title: [ABC News World] Spain holds state funeral for 69 killed in high-speed rail crash
item.description:
Spain holds state funeral for 69 killed in high-speed rail crash
Relatives of the 69 people killed in a high-speed rail collision in Spain last month attended a state funeral TuesdayByFRANCISCO SECO Associated Press and SUMAN NAISHADHAM Associated PressNovember 10, 2026, 2:16 PM
TOLEDO, Spain -- Relatives of the 69 people killed in a high-speed rail collision in Spain last month attended a state funeral on Tuesday with Spain's royals, almost two weeks after the crash.
The ceremony took place in the towering 13th-century Toledo Cathedral in central Spain.
The collision happened on Oct. 28 when a high-speed train slammed into another that was stationary on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda, around 140 kilometers (87 miles) south of the capital.
It was the second deadly collision this year involving Spain’s extensive high-speed rail network, shattering Spaniards' trust in the transit system that is regarded as one of the country's crowning achievements.
Under growing pressure, Transport Minister Óscar Puente stepped down last week. His resignation was followed by that of Luis Pedro Marco, who was head of Spain's railway infrastructure operator.
Spain will hold a general election on Nov. 29, in which progressive Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is seeking reelection.
Sánchez did not attend Tuesday's funeral service.
A 16th-century sculpture of Christ was moved from the town of Urda to the cathedral in Toledo for the funeral service.

Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities
Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent
Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.
The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.
“I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine. I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage,” Hamilton said in October.
A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day.
Israeli forces have continued to advance, expanding their control from 53% of the territory to at least 60%, an independent commission of UN experts said last month.
View image in fullscreen
Lewis Hamilton (in black) listens to an Egyptian Red Crescent official during a visit to a logistics centre in Al-Arish. Photograph: Mohammed Arafat/AP
Airstrikes also continue, and Israeli fire along the advancing front has killed at least 196 Palestinians, including 18 women, 32 boys and 11 girls, the commission said.
Hamilton toured Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with Gaza before visiting logistics warehouses operated by the Egyptian Red Crescent, which facilitates the entry of aid to Gaza.

Overnight strikes in Yemen kill at least 1 person and wound 9, and other Mideast news
Overnight strikes in Yemen have hit a gas station and an oil facility, killing at least one person and wounding nine othersByThe Associated PressNovember 10, 2026, 7:06 AM
Share
Overnight strikes hit a gas station and an oil facility in Yemen, killing at least one person and wounding nine, residents and the Iran-backed Houthi rebels said on Tuesday.
In Iran, a top security official claimed that the Iran war had already “wrecked” the United States, and called on Washington to accept seven demands that Tehran has made for an end to the conflict.
Here is the latest news from the Middle East on Tuesday. Read our full coverage here.
Houthi-run health ministry spokesperson Anees al-Asbahi said in a statement on X on Tuesday that a strike hit a gas station in a district of Yemen's capital, Sanaa, killing one person and wounding three others.
He said another airstrike targeted an oil company, wounding at least six people, causing “extensive damage” to nearby homes and shops and panicking residents.
Al-Asbahi blamed Saudi Arabia for both strikes. The Associated Press couldn’t independently verify his claims.
The strikes come amid renewed fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces that escalated this summer. The rebels continue to target Saudi energy facilities and airports as part of a campaign they say is meant to push Saudi Arabia into lifting its blockade on Yemen.
Sanaa resident Khaled al-Khawlani told the AP on Tuesday that he was horrified by the explosions that targeted the oil facility near residential areas of Sanaa at around 4 a.m.
Another resident said the explosions shattered his windows and reverberated across the city while people slept. The resident spoke on condition of anonymity for security reasons.

item.title: [BBC China] Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description:
Image source, Bloomberg via Getty ImagesByArchie MitchellBusiness reporterPublished9 November 2026
Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.
Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.
However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report, external.
The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Jensen Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.
The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week.

People at the scene of the collision in Giza province. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
People at the scene of the collision in Giza province. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images
Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo
Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said.
The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment.
Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways.
Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash occurred, said people rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances.
Gamal said he saw about 80 of the injured being taken by ambulances to hospital. Some passengers were trapped inside one of the carriages of the stationary train and died, he said.
View image in fullscreen
People search for survivors after the collision. Photograph: AP
Egypt’s president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi, said in a social media post that he had ordered a prompt investigation.

View image in fullscreen
Daniel Oyegade on the shoot for Homage, a See My World production. Photograph: Omar Balaa
How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester
See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives
African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.
See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.
The festival is part of See My World’s year-round programme showcasing pan-African arts, culture and events.
It reflects the determination among creatives and activists in Manchester to build on the legacy of the 1945 Pan-African Congress in Manchester – which connected luminaries of postwar independence movements with a shared vision of liberation – after last year’s 80th anniversary commemorations.
See My World’s CEO and artistic director, Tunde Adekoya, said this month’s film festival was taking inspiration from across the spectrum of pan-African thought, including the works of Kenyan writers John Mbiti, an Anglican theologian who died in 2019, and Ngũgĩ wa Thiong’o, the author of the groundbreaking 1986 book Decolonising the Mind who died last year.
Both writers rejected the colonial conceit that African thought was inferior, stressed the importance of community and saw reclaiming African ways of knowing as essential to a people’s self-understanding.

The building was one of 15 public housing towers in the coastal town of Caraballeda that collapsed in the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude quakes on June 24.
